ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, managers and UBOs against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, FATF public statements, and Luxembourg domestic AML/CFT enforcement lists. Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons in accordance with the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 and FATF Recommendation 12. UBO holdings above 25% must be verified, documented, and filed in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (LBR/RCS), https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in any language using the Latin alphabet. Names containing non-Latin script require a standardized French transliteration for registration. The official filing language for corporate documentation is French, with German and Luxembourgish accepted for court and administrative purposes.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bourse / Luxembourg Stock Exchange / Securities Exchange
Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File a renewal request through the LBR online portal before the original 90-day reservation expires. If the registrar refuses a proposed name, submit a written motivated objection to the Registrar within 15 days of the refusal notification. If the objection is denied, file an administrative appeal before the Tribunal Administratif within one month of the denial; a further appeal may be lodged with the Cour Administrative on questions of legal qualification or procedural error.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Pure virtual offices are not acceptable. A Luxembourg SARL must have a registered office in Luxembourg, which may be provided by a licensed domiciliation agent as a purely administrative seat. For active industrial manufacturing under ISIC 3240, a physical operational establishment with laser cutting and assembly facilities is mandatory and must be verifiable by authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% per annum low-to-moderate risk of unannounced on-site inspection by the Luxembourg Inspection du Travail, CSSF, social security authorities, and domiciliation verification agents.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 1-2, 100-1 to 100-25 (SARL provisions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association filed with the RCS and registered in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum subscribed capital for a SARL; at least 10% of the subscribed capital (with an absolute floor of EUR 12,000) must be deposited into a blocked escrow bank account in Luxembourg before the notarial deed is signed, and the blocked funds are released to the company only upon successful RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the Company’s subscribers accept and ratify the subscription of shares set forth in the Articles of Association, each quotaholder thereby contributing in cash or kind the agreed amounts to the SARL’s share capital; (2) that the registered office of the Company be established at [street and city], Luxembourg, and that this address be recorded with the Luxembourg Business Registers; (3) that [Name] and [Name] be, and each hereby is, appointed manager (gérant) of the Company, each with full authority to act and to represent the Company vis-à-vis third parties, jointly if required; (4) that the managers are authorized to open bank accounts, engage professional advisers, and complete all registration and licensing filings, including this first corporate governance act, as necessary to carry on the Company’s business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Clearance and Negative Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – RCS Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through the RCS Online web portal, specifying the desired corporate name, legal form (SARL), and proposed registered office. The registry checks against existing signs and distinctive marks; when clear, a negative certificate confirming name availability is issued.
required_dossiers: Copy of proposed corporate name and legal form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to identity or confusing similarity with an existing entity, submit a revised name incorporating a distinctive element or secondary trademark; the applicant may also request a written decision and file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Justice within 3 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Account Opening and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account at a Luxembourg bank in the name of the future company, deposit the minimum paid-in capital (at least EUR 12,000), and obtain a certificate of blocked funds (attestation de blocage) from the bank. The bank releases the funds only upon presentation of the RCS registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Negative certificate for the proposed company name
Passport or identity card of signatories and shareholders
Certificate of residence for non-resident shareholders
Bank account opening forms and AML/KYC declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional source-of-wealth documentation, provide sworn declaration and supporting bank statements; if a bank refuses due to internal AML policy, use an alternative bank and permit the notary to hold the capital equally until registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Signature of Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Luxembourg Chamber of Notaries)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the notarial deed of incorporation before the chosen Luxembourg notary. The notary authenticates the Articles of Association, verifies the escrow certificate and compliance with the 1915 Companies Law, and collects the signatures of the initial quotaholders and appointed managers.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all subscribers and managers
Personal or corporate shareholders’ residency/authorization documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a legal defect, amend the articles and convene a supplementary signature session within 48 hours; if a shareholder is unable to attend, grant a power of attorney authenticated by a Luxembourg consulate or Apostille formality.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized deed of incorporation along with the prescribed forms with the RCS, either electronically via RCS Online or physically at the RCS counter. The RCS assigns a business registration number and commits the company to the register; the amended deed is then published via the RESA electronic gazette.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation (original or first copy)
Payment of RCS statutory fee (approximately EUR 80)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or ancillary request, cure the requested rectification within 15 days through counsel; if the application is rejected, appeal to the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement) for an order directing registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration, Domains and VAT Administration (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA); National Social Security Centre (Centre commun de la sécurité sociale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SARL for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and VAT (in connection with e-commerce payments), and enroll with the Social Security Centre as an employer. This step finalizes the legal personality for commercial and payroll operations.
required_dossiers: Identification of effective managers and directors
Bank account details and anticipated turnover declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the competent tax office disagrees with the declared VAT effective date, provide a reconciliation of first invoices and bank records; if social security registration is delayed, obtain temporary employee coverage retroactively to the employment start date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) and the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploitation d'un établissement classé (Classe 1C – petite installation de fabrication)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: C2 – Registration/Declaration (Déclaration) for small-scale woodworking and CO2 laser cutting facility; full EIA Report not required below 1 tonne per day VOC emissions threshold and installed electrical capacity under 300 kW
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Luxembourg Regulation of 19 June 2009 on dangerous and unpleasant establishments; wood dust concentration below 5 mg/m³ at the worker exposure limit; VOC emissions below 5 kg/hour per unitary operation; wastewater discharges from wet scrubbers must meet pH 6-9, BOD5 below 25 mg/L, and total suspended solids below 30 mg/L; solid wood waste must be segregated as non-hazardous waste and delivered to authorized recyclers

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Corps (Service incendie et secours – SIS) covering premises and CO2 laser machinery; structural load inspection by the municipal authority confirming suitability of the existing floor for heavy equipment and storage; occupational health and safety clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) after verification of machine guards, emergency stops, local exhaust ventilation for fumes and dust, and laser-shielding compliance with the Luxembourg regulations on machinery safety; final clearance to operate is evidenced by a certificate of conformity from ITM and a fire safety opinion from the local commune.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct corporate income tax; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; national business e-government portal: Guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu; Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) for legal entity registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) is incorporated by notarial deed and registered with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL), obtaining a national business registration number. After incorporation and for VAT purposes, the entity must obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number. Resident established taxable persons apply for a VAT number through the AEDT/RCSL procedures, while non-resident taxable persons apply directly to the AEDT using the simplified VAT registration form; non-EU applicants may be required to appoint a VAT fiscal representative approved by the AEDT and provide security for potential VAT liabilities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not have US-style 'check-the-box' entity classification elections; the SARL is per se subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax as a capital company. Available statutory elections include: the option to form a VAT group under Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law for closely linked resident taxable persons; the option for corporate income tax consolidation under Article 164bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law for resident companies; and the application of the participation exemption through relevant anti-hybrid notifications, in compliance with ATAD/MLI hybrid mismatch rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for resident small enterprises under the Luxembourg franchise regime; no registration threshold for non-resident taxable persons supplying goods or services taxable in Luxembourg; EUR 10,000 Union distance-sales/OES threshold for intra-community distance selling and certain services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate real-time VAT clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping for domestic B2B invoices. E-invoicing is legally accepted if authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility are ensured. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2G supplies through the PEPPOL network and associated Luxembourg public-procurement portals. No fiscal API clearance or pre-clearance is imposed before invoice issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for VAT applies to supplies of goods dispatched or transported by the supplier, the customer, or a third party to a destination outside the European Union. Evidence must prove the goods physically left the EU within stated deadlines. Certain services related to exported goods (e.g., transport, ancillary services) and services directly tied to non-EU tangible movable property qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is established outside the EU or the service is effectively used wholly outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/ENS single administrative document or electronic export declaration)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR road consignment note evidencing physical export
Commercial invoice showing seller, buyer, description, export nature and terms
Proof of arrival / foreign customs clearance at destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank-based proof of export payment received from non-resident counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsupported or fraudulent zero-rating claims expose the taxpayer to immediate VAT clawback at 17% plus late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) and administrative penalties. Tax fraud or wrongful intent may trigger criminal penalties including fines and imprisonment under Articles 62 and 63 of the Luxembourg VAT Law. The AEDT may extend the ordinary reassessment limitation period from five years up to ten years where fraud or serious infringement is established; retrospective clawbacks may cover the full VAT amount, and indirect liability may extend to directors or fiscal representatives involved in improper export substantiation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting as the Eurosystem national central bank for monetary policy implementation and balance-of-payments statistics, with prudential and AML/CFT supervision of banks and payment/EMI institutions carried out by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). No bespoke foreign-exchange administration exists in Luxembourg; FX and capital-movement regulation is governed by EU law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. Luxembourg applies Article 63 TFEU (free movement of capital) and the OECD Capital Movements Code; current-account and capital-account operations are unrestricted. EUR receipts and foreign-currency balances may be freely converted, held in any currency, or repatriated without regulatory approval. Profit and dividend remittances face no FX conversion hurdle; the only frictions are fiscal and administrative: (i) the 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax, reduced to 0% for EU corporate shareholders meeting the Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions and further reduced or exempted under applicable double tax treaties; (ii) BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting for each cross-border financial transaction of EUR 12,500 or more; and (iii) the obligation to demonstrate genuine economic substance in Luxembourg to defend corporate tax residence and anti-abuse positions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio for export proceeds. Export collections may be retained indefinitely in any currency in any EU-authorized credit institution. The sole compliance overlay is the monthly BCL balance-of-payments statistics return: transactions with a given non-resident counterparty of at least EUR 12,500 must be declared under the goods-export category (BPM6 line 1.A.B.1), and supporting SEPA/SWIFT advices and Amazon Pay/Stripe settlement reports must be retained for five years under the AML law of 12 November 2004, as amended.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) for SARL incorporation deposit; EUR Operational Current Account; sub-account for Amazon Pay/Stripe collection sweeps
Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué); EUR Operational Account; documentary credit (L/C) and trade-finance services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué); EUR Operational Account with dedicated SME commercial banking package and e-banking gateway

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — conditional, secondary-rail only. Under PSD2 as transposed by the Luxembourg Law of 1 April 2019, CSSF-authorised and EEA-passported EMIs (e.g., Qonto, Revolut Business, Wise Business) may open corporate accounts with fully remote KYC. For this SARL, an EMI is legally viable as a low-limit collections and disbursements conduit for Amazon Pay/Stripe sweeps and supplier refunds, but it must not serve as the sole settlement bank because: (i) e-money float is not covered by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee fund (FGDL) and benefits only from safeguarding arrangements; (ii) credit facilities and documentary L/C capacity are unavailable or materially restricted; (iii) TARGET2 RTGS participation and high-value SWIFT MT103 processing are not offered; and (iv) BCL balance-of-payments reporting becomes fragmented across custodians, increasing compliance cost. Recommended architecture: Tier-1 Luxembourg bank for escrow, settlement, and trade finance; one EEA EMI for operational float, swept daily to the Tier-1 account via SEPA Instant Credit Transfer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Conditional mandate. Remote video identification is lawful in Luxembourg under CSSF e-KYC guidance (CSSF Circular 20/744 and subsequent FAQ statements) when performed via an eIDAS-qualified digital identity (e.g., Luxembourg eID, itsme) or a CSSF-accepted video-verification provider. A non-EU/EEA-resident gérant may therefore be onboarded entirely remotely if the bank's internal enhanced-due-diligence model accepts foreign-controlled manufacturing SMEs. In practice, however, the initial onboarding of a newly incorporated, non-resident-owned SARL triggers enhanced due diligence, and the majority of Tier-1 Luxembourg banks still require at least one in-person interview at a Luxembourg branch for the gérant or an EU-resident signatory holding a Luxembourg tax card, together with verification of the registered office. Consequently, the blueprint assumes one director or attorney visit to Luxembourg City for notarization, bank interview, and signature-card execution within 30 days of incorporation, with full remote opening treated as a fallback only.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-company and treaty-shopping indicator: newly incorporated SARL with 100% non-resident ownership and no domestic credit history, seeking immediate cross-border flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized articles of association; RCS extract (extrait du registre de commerce) dated within 3 months; Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) filing excerpt; CCSS (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale) employer registration; tax-file opening acknowledgment from the Administration des contributions directes; lease agreement for Luxembourg registered office; staffing plan and payroll evidence; laser-assembly facility lease or purchase agreement; business plan quantifying wood-puzzle production volumes; Amazon Seller Central and Stripe merchant identifiers; CE/EN-71 toy-safety and laser-machine operating certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for the minimum statutory share capital (EUR 12,000 for a standard SARL, 25% payable at incorporation) and any shareholder advances or capital contributions beyond the subscription price.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notary's deposit certificate (attestation de consignation) for the blocked capital account; original SWIFT MT103 or SEPA credit transfer from the shareholder; six months of bank statements of the contributing shareholder; signed source-of-wealth declaration from each UBO; apostilled and notarized passport copies; board or shareholder resolution authorizing the contribution; all non-French/German/English documents translated by a Luxembourg sworn translator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media flags on non-EU (e.g., PRC or Hong Kong connected) UBOs, directors, or export counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed CSSF-compliant KYC and PEP attestation forms for each UBO and signatory; World-Check and LexisNexis negative-news search reports showing no relevant hits; EU/UN/OFAC/UK OFSI sanctions screening certificates; apostilled passport copies and proof of address; legal-opinion letter from local counsel confirming no affiliation with sanctioned or restricted entities; written commitment to continuous transaction monitoring and periodic re-KYC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-model mismatch: corporate object in precision laser manufacturing and educational toys versus heavy e-commerce settlement strings (Amazon Pay, Stripe), raising marketplace-fraud or trade-based-laundering concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Amazon Services Europe Business Solutions Agreement and Stripe Merchant Agreement; at least 60 days of historical payout reports if the business is migrating, or a granular pro-forma cash-flow model if new; Luxembourg VAT registration certificate; marketplace product listings demonstrating genuine B2C/B2B toy sales; customs import/export declarations for wood panels and laser components; product-liability insurance and CE/EN-71 quality certificates; daily three-way reconciliation policy mapping Amazon/Stripe settlements to the operating account and sales invoices.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the initial and any subsequent equity contributions: (i) the Luxembourg notary identifies the precise subscription amount (minimum EUR 12,000 for a standard SARL); (ii) the foreign shareholder executes a SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA-resident shareholders) to the SARL's blocked capital account at the Tier-1 bank, citing purpose code 'Direct investment — equity capital' under the BCL balance-of-payments BPM6 classification, the SARL's name, RCS provisional registration number, and the notary's file reference; (iii) following RCS registration, the bank converts the blocked account into the operational current account upon presentation of the notarial attestation of deposit and registered-office confirmation; (iv) every inward transaction of EUR 12,500 or more must be declared on the BCL monthly balance-of-payments return, with full SWIFT text, notarial certificate, share register excerpt, and source-of-funds documentation retained for five years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing hierarchy for procurement and operating expenses: (i) EEA-domiciled suppliers — SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (sub-10-second settlement) for payments up to EUR 100,000; (ii) high-value EU payments requiring finality — TARGET2 (T2) RTGS through the Luxembourg bank's e-banking gateway with dual-authorization; (iii) non-EEA suppliers (Chinese laser-tube and optical-component vendors, wood-panel importers) — SWIFT MT103 priority wire, or an irrevocable confirmed at-sight documentary letter of credit (UCP 600) for contract values above EUR 50,000, with the Luxembourg confirming bank settling against presented shipping and airway documents; (iv) e-commerce collection rails: Amazon EU S.à r.l. remits EUR sales proceeds via SEPA Credit Transfer to the operating account, and Stripe (settling via Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd., an Irish EMI) forwards EUR balances by SEPA; (v) all vendor payments are executed exclusively through the bank's corporate SWIFT/e-banking channel with a two-signatory approval matrix and no third-party payment processors on the operating account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable spot and outright FX forwards (tenors up to 12 months, trade-support documentation required; NDF not applicable because EUR is fully convertible)
EUR/GBP deliverable spot and outright FX forwards (hedging Amazon.co.uk net sales exposure)
EUR/CNH deliverable FX forwards via offshore renminbi market (covering mainland China raw-material and equipment payables)
Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars/risk reversals (board-approved, premium funded from operational cash flow only)
Cross-currency swap (EUR/USD) for future intercompany financing or trade-credit lines denominated in USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (LBR/RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month following each anniversary of the entity's RCS registration date, ending on the last day of that month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers administrative fine up to EUR 5,000; two consecutive years of missing confirmation expose the SARL to an RCS warning (mise en demeure) and administrative strike-off (radiation d'office).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) and publication in RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS) and official electronic publications platform (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year end, the filing deadline is 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file allows the tribunal de commerce to order filing under a coercive periodic fine (astreinte); additional administrative penalties up to EUR 25,000 and individual criminal sanctions for directors may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT), and net wealth tax (NWT) declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 May of the year following the relevant tax year; a filing extension to 31 December is generally available upon electronic submission or prior request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing results in default interest at 0.8% per month on any unpaid tax, a late-filing penalty of up to EUR 1,500 per return, and possible official tax assessment by the ACD followed by enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), administered by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after each anniversary of the initial RBE registration; any shareholder or UBO data change must additionally be notified within one month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-response to the annual confirmation triggers administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and up to 6 months of imprisonment for intentional omission by directors or managers; repeat breaches may lead to RCS strike-off procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) if it exceeds two of the three legal thresholds: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 4.4 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million, and average annual employee headcount exceeding 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 as amended by the Law of 19 December 2015 transposing Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is required for listed companies and may be voluntarily applied for consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SARL must file an annual RBE confirmation on the anniversary of its initial RBE registration, irrespective of any shareholding change; the confirmation is submitted through the RBE e-filing portal by a director or authorised signatory and certifies that recorded beneficial-owner data remains accurate. Any transfer of shares or alteration in UBO particulars must be separately filed within one month, along with an updated internal beneficial-owner register.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - 3,000 per year for registered office services and professional corporate agent support in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 8,000 per year when statutory audit threshold is exceeded; nil for exempt small SARL
